description: We are 213 Technic, a team focused on aerospace, space technologies, software, and innovative engineering. We have experience in rocket design, simulation, structural analysis, and aerospace software. We are looking for motivated members with skills in programming, data analysis, aerospace engineering, or research. Join us to build an impactful space-focused project together!
summary:
We built 213 HealthCare (by Team 213 Technic), a 100% offline browser-based astronaut health monitoring and 3D digital twin application. Designed for Earth-independent medical operations (EIMO) in a clinical Flight-Ops Editorial UI, it gathers simulated wearable and cabin indicators, evaluates them against NASA-STD-3001 thresholds, and prescribes countermeasures when communication delays reach 24 light-minutes.

A Three.js 3D anatomical twin (morphable GLB rig with GLSL X-ray shaders and 5 clickable organ hotspots) synchronizes with synthetic Bio-Monitor waveforms (ECG, ABP, RIP respiration, EtCO2), EchoFinder-2 ultrasound/OCT guides with local device image review, and animated ARED/T2/CEVIS/LBNP countermeasure protocols. It pairs microgravity aware clinical gating Space Fever CRP/WBC/SQI antibiotic checks, HOMA-IR insulin resistance, and cabin ppCO2 monitoring (<= 3.0 mmHg) with CHeCS medication caps, NASA EER nutrition, AMS-18/spatial/risk cognition tests, UTC reminders, and DTN store an forward queuing. Open-source under Apache 2.0 (SI units; SIMULATED TELEMETRY labels; no NASA insignia).
details:
What It Does & How It Works

213 HealthCare is an offline-first, bilingual (EN/TR, defaulting to EN) astronaut health monitoring web application developed by Team 213 Technic, uniting four integrated views:

1. Astronaut 3D Tablet: An interactive Three.js (r128) digital twin loads a local morphable GLB rig (parametric-base.glb with runtime binary morph-target trimming, CPU linear-blend skinning, merged vertices, male/female morph weights, and custom GLSL Fresnel X-ray shaders) featuring five clickable organ hotspots (Cardiovascular, Bone/BMD, Immune, Neuro-Ocular, Respiratory). Alongside the 3D twin, a live Vitals Monitor plots synthetic physiological waveforms (McSharry Gaussian-sum ECG across 0G sinus, NSVT, AFib, QT prolongation, and hypercapnic tachycardia states, plus ABP, RIP respiration, and EtCO2). An interactive Action Center renders 2D Canvas countermeasure animations (ARED, T2 COLBERT, CEVIS + LBNP -25 mmHg, Chibis fluid loading, ECLSS CDRA ventilation, 480 nm SSLA circadian LED + breathing, and water-wall shielding) and an EchoFinder-2 Just in Time ultrasound/OCT guide (Heart/IJV, Kidney/Bladder, and OCT Retina with local-only image review never uploaded).

2. Flight Surgeon Console: Displays NASA-STD-3001 KPI cards (Adaptation Z-score, Cabin ppCO2 <= 3.00 mmHg [V2 6004], HR/HRV/BMD loss, Sensor SQI < 40% gate), a 180-day Adaptation Tunnel SVG (Hughson 2012 envelope), ppCO2 correlation wave, 5-hazard RIDGE radar, and CUSUM action log with animated countermeasure previews.

3. Mobile Terminal & Crew Care Modules: Covers 4 mission environments (ISS LEO, Deep Space Transit, Planetary Rover EVA, Lunar 0.16G / Mars 0.38G Habitat up to 24.0-min OWLT) with automatic sensor synchronization (BP, HR, Glucose, HOMA-IR, Stahn 2017 ~38.0 C Space Fever baseline drift, ~8.5 h sleep [V1 4011], Mood 1-5) plus manual overrides. It runs automated CDSS rules (antibiotic therapy locked unless CRP HIGH + WBC HIGH + SQI >= 40%), provides Plain vs. Clinical 5-question crew explanations, tracks real UTC streaks/badges, and queues telemetry packets in a Disruption-Tolerant Networking (DTN) store-and-forward buffer with Solar Blackout simulation. Integrated Crew Care Modules cover AMS-18 + Spatial + Risk cognition tests, NASA EER nutrition & shelf-life/Veggie tracking, and CHeCS medication safety limits (Ibuprofen 3,200 mg/day cap, Diaz 2024 expiration alerts).

4. NASA Evidence & Medication Center: A 12-tab reference library documenting formulas, CHeCS drug tables, Red Risks, 3-Tier Hybrid engineering comparisons, CSA Bio-Monitor hardware specs (250 Hz ECG, 125 Hz RIP, 75 Hz PPG, 1 Hz SpO2/temp, 50 Hz +/-16 g IMU, NASA-STD-6016, MIL-STD-461, EPCE <= 0.5 mA), Flight TRL 7-9 vs. Ground TRL 2-3 honesty matrix, OWLT/DTN autonomy, and 50+ primary citations. Top-bar utilities add mission scenario presets, custom scenario creation, live threshold notifications, UTC schedule reminders, and print/PDF clinical reports.

Benefits & Intended Impact

As missions extend from LEO toward Artemis lunar habitats and Mars (4-24 min one-way light time), ground flight surgeons cannot provide synchronous triage. 213 HealthCare translates passive telemetry into crew-executable triage, drug expiration/dosing guardrails, nutrition adequacy checks, and osteogenic/cardiovascular countermeasures—reducing cognitive burden, preventing false terrestrially calibrated alarms, and operating with zero cloud dependency.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software

- Frontend Stack: Pure HTML5, CSS3 (Clinical Instrument / Flight-Ops Editorial design system), and vanilla ES6+ modular JavaScript bundled for 100% offline execution under Apache 2.0.

- Bundled Open-Source Libraries (local vendor/): React 18.3.1 & ReactDOM 18.3.1 (MIT), Three.js r128 with OrbitControls, GLTFLoader, BufferGeometryUtils (MIT), Tailwind CSS 3.4.17, and local Fontsource .woff2 fonts (SIL OFL 1.1: Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono, Orbitron, Rajdhani, Inter).

- Anatomical Assets: Local parametric morphable GLB rig (parametric-base.glb) plus bundled NIH Visible Human Project / HuBMAP CCF v1.2 cryosection mesh module (CC BY 4.0).

- Hardware Context: Modeled around ISS CSA Bio-Monitor wearable specs (Flight TRL 7-9), ARED, T2 COLBERT, CEVIS/LBNP, CDRA, SSLA lighting, and EchoFinder-2 ultrasound—runs in any standard desktop/tablet browser with WebGL and 0 network dependency.

Creativity & Key Engineering Factors

- Microgravity-Specific Physiology: Accounts for 0G Space Fever (~38.0 C baseline vs. terrestrial 37.0 C), cephalic fluid shifts, HOMA-IR metabolic trends, and hypercapnic CO2-pocket headache risk (ppCO2 <= 3.0 mmHg) rather than misapplying Earth norms.

- Operational Safety & Realism: Enforces Signal Quality Index (SQI >= 40%) gating before automated alerts/antibiotics, pairs clinical terminology with plain-language astronaut explanations, keeps uploaded medical images strictly local on-device, uses SI units throughout, and marks all synthetic waveforms SIMULATED TELEMETRY.

- Scientific, Legal & AI (SI) Transparency: Grounded in NASA-STD-3001, HRP Red Risks, CSA data, and peer-reviewed studies with zero NASA insignia. AI assistants supported code implementation, debugging, reference structuring, and EN/TR translation during development; all runtime medical logic is deterministic (no runtime AI/ML model).
